issues.legal_issue: A notification reserving land for non-agricultural or industrial development makes the tenancy regime inapplicable to that land retrospectively, so a rent determination under that regime does not bar a civil court from determining rent, subject to preserved legacy tenant rights.
material_facts: The tenant took possession of the land under a lease beginning in 1956, after the 1948 tenancy statute had been extended to the area.
In 1958, the State Government issued a notification reserving land within the relevant municipal limits for non-agricultural or industrial development.
A Mamlatdar had determined rent for the land under sections 8 and 9 of the 1948 statute.
The landlord brought a civil suit to recover rent, and the civil court determined reasonable rent after the High Court directed it to do so.
The tenant’s asserted right to the rent fixed by the Mamlatdar arose under the 1948 statute, rather than from protected-tenant status preserved under the 1939 statute.
issues.conclusion: The notification made the 1948 statute inapplicable to the land retrospectively, subject to the statutory exception for preserved legacy rights. The Mamlatdar’s rent determination therefore became ineffective, and the civil court was competent to determine reasonable rent. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 88(1)(b), 89(2)(b), and 89A of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, read together, make the statute inapplicable to land specified by a reservation notification, notwithstanding the general preservation of accrued rights in section 89(2)(b); section 89A preserves the specified protected-tenant rights arising under sections 3, 3A, and 4 of the Bombay Tenancy Act, 1939. Mohanlal Chunilal Kothari v. Tribhovan Haribhai Tamboli supports the retrospective effect of a reservation notification; Sidram Narsappa Kamble v. Sholapur Borough Municipality supports the limited preservation of protected-tenant rights. Sakharam @ Bapusaheb Narayan Sanas v. Manikchand Motichand Shah was distinguished because it did not concern a notification under section 88(1)(b).

rule.if: civil_rent_recovery_proceeding and land_reserved_by_notification and rent_fixed_under_displaced_tenancy_regime and not tenant_has_preserved_legacy_status

predicates.civil_rent_recovery_proceeding: A civil court is hearing a dispute about rent payable for land.
predicates.land_reserved_by_notification: The State Government has officially specified the land as reserved for non-agricultural or industrial development.
predicates.rent_fixed_under_displaced_tenancy_regim: A rent determination for the land was made under a tenancy regime that no longer applies to the land.
predicates.tenant_has_preserved_legacy_status: The tenant has protected-tenant status preserved from the predecessor tenancy regime.

issues.definition: When a civil court hears a rent dispute concerning land reserved by notification and rent was fixed under a tenancy regime displaced for that land, the civil court may determine rent if the tenant lacks preserved legacy status.
